title: Customer network change contract and evidence capsule (PRD - WIP)
content:
Purpose and problem statement:
This draft proposes a compact, verifiable "evidence capsule" format and an accompanying contract model for describing customer-managed network changes in Redwood Private deployments. The goal is to provide: (1) a machine-readable canonical audit record that both Redwood and the customer can independently verify; (2) a standardized approval-gate model that maps to customer policies and operator actions; and (3) pragmatic retention and retrieval semantics that satisfy compliance requests while minimizing storage and privacy exposure.

Why this matters now:
- Customers increasingly require evidence of who changed what, when, and why across VPC, firewall, and on-prem connectors to meet compliance and internal governance.
- Current ad-hoc logs are fragmented (console, ticket references, emails) and hard to use during incident response or for regulatory audits.
- We need a cross-team specification (product, SRE, infra, legal) to align API surfaces, operational tooling, and retention guarantees.

High-level approach and constraints:
- Create an "evidence capsule": a compact JSON-LD-like blob that contains a minimal canonical representation of a change event and cryptographic references (signed hashes) rather than full binary attachments where possible.
- Capsules are append-only objects stored in Redwood-managed audit storage for Hosted/Dedicated, and exported/anchored for Private as per customer contract (customer can choose export/escrow).
- Approval gates map to policy predicates (automated policy allow/deny), operator attestation (manual approval), and external attestation (customer-signed assertion).
- Privacy constraint: PII in capsules should be redacted or hashed according to customer policy; raw configuration diffs can be stored in customer-controlled escrow if required.

Evidence capsule schema (proposed fields):
- capsule_id (string): UUID v4
- change_id (string): human-friendly short id (e.g., C-20241003-0001)
- timestamp_utc (string): ISO8601
- initiator (string): principal id (redwood:user:123 or customer:alice@acme.com)
- subject_scope (string): e.g., "vpc/peer-attachment/v1"
- delta_summary (string): short human summary (max 512 chars)
- diff_hash (string): sha256 of the canonical diff payload (stored separately if large)

(continued)
- attachment_refs (list of strings): URLs or content-hash references for supporting artifacts (ticket id, console snapshot, customer config file)
- approvals (list of approval objects serialized as strings): each approval object fields flattened as "approver|role|time|method|signature_ref"
- approval_policy_id (string): internal policy id that evaluated the change, if any
- operator_attested (string): "true" | "false" (simple flattening to comply with no nested objects constraint)
- prev_capsule_ref (string): capsule_id of previous related change (for chains)
- evidence_root (string): merkle root or anchored proof reference (e.g., ledger hash)
- retention_profile (string): e.g., "7d-ephemeral", "90d-standard", "customer-escrow-indefinite"
- redact_level (string): "none" | "partial" | "full" (indicates PII redaction policy applied)
- operator_notes (string): free text for ops (max 2000 chars)
- integrity_signature (string): base64 signature over canonicalized capsule by Redwood private key or customer key when available

Approval gates model (conceptual):
- Gate types:
  1) Policy-automated: change evaluated by policy engine (e.g., allowed by route/whitelist). Capsule includes policy id and verdict.
  2) Operator-manual: human in loop; the operator must attest. Evidence capsule includes operator signature and justification.
  3) Customer-signed: customer operator service posts a signed assertion (useful for customer-managed change where customer wants the canonical identity).
  4) Out-of-band legal/consensus: changes that require contractual sign-off (rare) documented by proof references.

Approval sequence examples (flattened):
- Quick auto-approve path: Policy-automated -> capsule with approval_policy_id set -> integrity_signature by Redwood -> stored -> retention_profile="90d-standard"
- Customer-managed path: Customer submits change -> Customer signs capsule (integrity_signature) -> Redwood ingests capsule and anchors evidence_root -> operator does a lightweight validation -> operator_attested="true" -> retention_profile set per contract (e.g., escrow)
- Escalation path: Policy denies -> ticket auto-generated -> manual operator-review required -> operator attests or requests customer-signed override -> approval recorded in capsule.approvals

API surfaces (draft):
- POST /private/v1/evidence-capsules  (body: capsule JSON with attachment_refs or diff_hash) -> returns capsule_id, ingestion_status
- GET /private/v1/evidence-capsules/{capsule_id} -> returns capsule metadata and authorized attachment_refs (signed short-lived URLs)
- POST /private/v1/evidence-capsules/{capsule_id}/approve -> operator/customer can submit approval token/signature (method param: operator | customer | policy)
- GET /private/v1/evidence-capsules?filter=change_id|initiator|time-range&cursor= -> list for audit export (CSV/NDJSON)
- POST /private/v1/evidence-export/{contract_id} -> request escrow export (ZIP of capsules)

Operational considerations:
- Ingestion latency SLO: < 500ms for metadata ingestion; attachments may be async (background fetch/anchoring).
- Searchability: index capsule metadata fields (initiator, change_id, subject_scope, approval_policy_id) for fast queries. Avoid indexing full diffs unless consented.
- Anchoring: Evidence roots should be anchored periodically to an immutable ledger (internal or external) for non-repudiation.
- Escrow/export: customers may ask to push raw diffs to customer-controlled S3 or to a third-party escrow provider. Ensure encryption-in-transit and at-rest, and an auditable handoff record (capsule with export_ref).

Retention profiles and GDPR/CCPA considerations:
- Profiles: ephemeral-7d, standard-90d, extended-365d, escrow-indefinite. Default for Private is defined by contract.
- Right to erasure: when a customer requests deletion, we must either delete full capsule (if escrowed elsewhere) or redact PII fields and record an erasure event capsule (for non-repudiation).
- Access controls: RBAC via token scopes; support cross-tenant read for SRE on-call with justification audit trail.

Telemetry and monitoring:
- Ingest metrics: capsules_ingested_total, capsule_ingest_latency_ms_p95, attachment_processing_failures_total
- Audit retrieval metrics: export_requests_total, export_success_rate, export_latency_p50/p95
- Quality signals: capsules_missing_approval_ratio, capsules_with_unanchored_evidence_total
- Alerts: missing anchoring for >24h, escrow export failures, ingestion error spike

Rollout and migration plan (phased):
1) Internal pilot (2 weeks): enable for Redwood-managed Dedicated networks only; validate capsule schema and anchoring flow.
2) Beta with two customers (6–8 weeks): opt-in in Private deployments; provide escrow export to customer S3.
3) GA: default evidence ingestion enabled for all Private customers with contractual options for retention and escrow.

Success metrics (examples):
- 95% of change events captured as evidence capsules within 1 minute of change
- Export retrieval time <= 30s for audit bundles under 100MB
- Customer satisfaction: NPS target for audit experience +10 after GA

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: storing diffs with secrets. Mitigation: default redaction + customer-controlled escrow that retains raw diffs.
- Risk: compliance expectations vary widely. Mitigation: provide flexible retention profiles and export/escrow options; include legal early.
- Risk: operator burden. Mitigation: automate policy decisions and provide clear operator UI for attestation.

Open questions / items for next iteration:
- Canonical diff format: YAML patch vs. binary delta? (engineering input needed)
- Signing model: do we require customer public keys in onboarding flow, or support ad-hoc signed JWTs?
- Anchoring cadence: hourly vs daily — tradeoffs for cost and resolution.
- How do we surface capsule chains in the Console UI for easy inspection?

Next steps (owners):
- Product: finalize schema choices and retention profile names (owner: Maya) - due 2024-11-15
- Eng infra: prototype ingestion API and anchoring stub (owner: Ravi) - due 2024-12-05
- Legal: draft contract language for escrow and retention (owner: Sofia) - due 2024-11-22
- SRE: outline runbooks for retrieval and incident response using capsules (owner: Ethan) - due 2024-12-01

Appendix: short example capsule (flattened for storage):

approvals: ["ops-lead|operator|2024-10-03T18:24:02Z|console|sigref:sgn-4321","policy|automated|2024-10-03T18:22:31Z|policy-engine|sigref:sgn-4320"]

(end)

This document is intentionally written as a working draft to capture the product and engineering tradeoffs. Feedback welcome — add comments inline or ping me in #private-deployments.
content_summary: Draft describing a proposed "evidence capsule" schema and contract model for customer-managed network changes in Redwood Private deployments; includes schema, approval models, API surfaces, operational and legal considerations, rollout plan, and example capsule.
